text:
Blake Lizotte has no goals in 17 games, and he's had chances for about two: 2.26 expected goals on 18 shots. It's the kind of drought that a fourth-line center can live with as long as the rest of his game holds, and for the most part it has. Pittsburgh takes 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, nearly four points better than without him.

He isn't on the ice to score. He's undrafted, out of St. Cloud State, and his role is checking minutes, the penalty kill and blocked shots (19 already). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season does find a skill worth watching: 8.2 primary shot assists per 60 minutes, 84th percentile among forwards. He sets up more than he shoots.

His minutes are up slightly over his last ten games. We project about 30 points and 8 goals, which assumes the shooting catches up to a normal rate. For a Penguins team that has lost the chance battle often this season, a bottom-six center winning his shifts is useful, goals or not. The first one is coming.
headline: Lizotte, still looking for one
